text:
Michael Brandsegg-Nygård has 102 hits in 22 games. Read that again. The 21-year-old Norwegian, Detroit's 15th overall pick in 2024, has turned his first full NHL season into a nightly physical event, and he's added 4 goals and 11 points on about 15 and a half minutes.

The goals should be higher. He's had 7.3 expected goals of chances (that's a lot for his role) and converted four, so our numbers list him as due. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, had him finishing off the most dangerous passes, across the slot or from behind the net, at a rate that suits a shooter with a top-10% shot by speed. Detroit gets about 53% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, almost five points better than without him, though some of the goal differential in his minutes has come from friendly goaltending.

For context, forwards drafted 10th to 20th since 2005 scored a median 0.35 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.50. Watch the shot totals on the Red Wings' bad nights. The looks keep coming, and those tend to turn into goals.
